title: Data centres, water security and health
summary: Negotiate public-health safeguards for digital infrastructure: cooling water, reliable power, transparent evidence and fair financing.

packet.background: Data centres require electricity; water use can arise in cooling and upstream electricity generation. Impacts depend on technology, climate, location and the electricity mix. The negotiating setting below is fictional: governments are considering shared public-health recommendations while water and grid capacity face competing demands.
packet.objective: Agree a recommendation covering water disclosure, drought safeguards, essential health services, equitable financing and measurable implementation. Distinguish water withdrawal from consumption and direct from indirect use.
packet.scope: Original ASSEMBLY exercise, not an official WHO agenda item or a replica of an announced GMWHO 2026 topic. All countries, mandates and events are fictional. WHO recommendations do not themselves grant or revoke national data-centre permits.
